chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man marries a woman, then is secluded with her, closes the door upon her, and lowers the curtain, then divorces her, the dowry becomes obligatory, and her seclusion with him is considered consummation (dakhul).

key_terms.الصَّدَاقُ: The dowry or mahr given to the wife
key_terms.خَلَاؤُهَا بِهَا: Seclusion of the wife with the husband

ai.seo_question: Does seclusion count as consummation for the full dowry if no intercourse occurred?
ai.summary: In al-istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this chain to establish that 'khuluw' (seclusion) serves as a legal proxy for consummation, a principle central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the fullness of the dowry (mahr). This ruling highlights the significance of privacy and the potential for intimacy in marital contracts, distinguishing it from cases where divorce occurs before any form of seclusion.
